thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-gpu-pool utilization 98% | queue_depth=1242 | avg_enqueue_latency=2.8s | error_rate=4.2% — paging oncall

alice_sre: Got it — paging @bob_oncall and @carol_runtime. Creating bridge now. :rotating_light:

bob_oncall: I'm on it. Seeing queue climb, autoscaler has stuck at 60 nodes (max=60). Scaling attempts hit quota error: "max_nodes_reached". Can we temporarily raise max?

carol_runtime: Also seeing repeated Xid errors on several nodes in west-eu-2. dmesg shows `NVRM: Xid (13): PID 0` on three hosts. That likely reduces effective GPUs.

alice_sre: Customer impact: multiple heavy tenants reporting >3s tail latency and intermittent 429s. CS alerted @eve_cs.

eve_cs: FYI I already opened a CS ticket for two customers on enterprise plans. They're seeing request timeouts and are asking if we're aware. Keeping them updated.

frank_eng: Quick check: any recent driver rollouts? deploy-bot did a driver bump ~2h ago to 535.86 on prod-gpu-pool.

deploy-bot: deploy: driver-rollout/prod-gpu-pool @535.86 completed 2h ago (canary 5 nodes -> full). Logs: no immediate rollback.

bob_oncall: That aligns. Let's pin hypothesis: driver rollout caused instability -> nodes flapping -> autoscaler perceives healthy pool but usable GPUs reduced -> queue piles up -> autoscaler hits max_nodes (we hit our configured upper bound) -> queue backpressure and throttling.

carol_runtime: Confirmed nodes in podset 'gpu-west-eu-2-a' are flapping. kubectl logs on runtime-agent:

```
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z runtime-agent[pid=820]: ERROR nvml: device 2: Xid 13 detected
2026-03-15T10:02:13Z runtime-agent[pid=820]: WARN eviction: restoring device state failed
2026-03-15T10:02:14Z runtime-agent[pid=820]: INFO node-status: marking dev2 degraded
```

carol_runtime: nvidia-smi on one host shows multiple processes in Z state and GPU memory not freeing.

```
$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 535.86 Driver Version: 535.86 | GPU-Util 98% | Memory-Usage 92%
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Processes:  82 | Zombie: 12 | 
```

alice_sre: Immediate mitigation options — list and prioritize:
- emergency-burst: request +15 nodes from capacity pool (if available) — requires infra approval
- roll back driver to 535.79 on canary -> full if stable
- cordon+evict flapping nodes to stop thrash and let autoscaler replace
- raise autoscaler max_nodes to 80 temporarily
- enable model-fallback routing -> route heavy requests to smaller model variants to reduce GPU memory

bob_oncall: I'm starting with cordon+evict on obviously flapping nodes (ids: gpu-weu-12, gpu-weu-14, gpu-weu-19). Will then try raising max_nodes to 80. Executing now.

frank_eng: If you raise max_nodes, we should also throttle burst to avoid pulling more nodes into the same bad driver state.

bob_oncall: Executed:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-weu-12
kubectl drain gpu-weu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
autoscalerctl set max-nodes prod-gpu-pool 80 --expires 1h
```

incident-bot: ACTION: autoscaler.max_nodes updated to 80 by bob_oncall at 5256789600

carol_runtime: Eviction logs show kernel panic on gpu-weu-14 during drain: `kernel: NVRM: Xid (13): GPU access fault` — node forced reboot. That's expected but reduces usable capacity briefly.

alice_sre: I've asked infra to approve emergency-burst. @dan_product, any constraints on burst for enterprise SLAs?

dan_product: We can approve emergency burst for 2h for impacted regions. Notify billing for overage. Approving +10 nodes for west-eu.

frank_eng: Rolling back driver on canary nodes first. Canary set id: canary-gpu-7. Rolling to 535.79 now.

Deploy-bot (note: case in thread uses deploy-bot earlier as lowercase): deploy-bot: deploy: driver-rollback/canary-gpu-7 -> 535.79 initiated by frank_eng

bob_oncall: Post-eviction: queue depth dropped from 1242 -> 780 in 8m. Error rate still ~2.1%. Tail latency improving but not fully recovered.

carol_runtime: After rollback on canary, canary host stable for 6m. No new Xid logs. Starting staged rollback on 10 nodes with 30s spacing.

frank_eng: Also enabling model-fallback for two large routes:
```
redwood-route update --route heavy-gen --fallback-model small-gen-v1 --percent=50
redwood-route update --route batch-embed --fallback-model embed-quant-v2 --percent=100
```

alice_sre: Good. Customer visible symptoms should reduce as requests get routed. Eve, keep customers updated: let them know mitigation in progress and ETA ~30-45m.

eve_cs: Noted. Messaging draft: "We are mitigating increased latency by routing some traffic to alternative model variants and adding capacity; a fix is being rolled out. We'll follow up in 30m." Sending now.

bob_oncall: Autoscaler increase succeeded and we got +6 new nodes from reserved pool; emergency-burst +10 still pending due to quota.

incident-bot: NOTE: quota-api returned 429 for emergency-burst request; infra is resolving with cloud-provider support.

carol_runtime: After further reboots and cordons, we still see two hosts with repeated Xid on reboot loop — likely hardware/driver interplay; isolating them from pool now.

frank_eng: Continuing driver rollback across pool; monitoring kernel logs. LP: check GPU BIOS differences — some of the west-eu machines are still on varied BIOS versions; mismatch might expose driver bugs at scale.

alice_sre: Action item roundup before handoff:
- driver rollback to 535.79 across pool (in progress) — frank_eng
- isolate suspect hosts: gpu-weu-14, gpu-weu-19 — bob_oncall/carol_runtime
- autoscaler max_nodes = 80 for 1h (revert scheduled) — bob_oncall
- emergency-burst +10 (infra follow-up) — alice_sre/infra
- customer comms updates every 30m — eve_cs
- monitor queue and error rates; lower fallback percentages if stable — frank_eng

bob_oncall: Creating follow-up ticket: INC-2026-9247 with all logs and timeline. Handoff to night oncall: @grace_oncall — summary pinned in ticket.

grace_oncall: Acknowledged. I'll join the bridge at handoff and take over monitoring. Any outstanding risks?

alice_sre: Outstanding: emergency-burst still pending; two hosts in reboot loop may need replacement; keep an eye on autoscaler oscillation if rollback isn't complete.

frank_eng: Early post-rollback metrics: usable GPU count increased from 42 -> 58 (after rollout stage 1) and average enqueue latency down to 1.2s. We'll continue rollout until stability confirmed.

eve_cs: Customers updated. One enterprise requested a bridge; scheduling a 1:1 with their ops team in 40m.

bob_oncall: Handoff time 5256792600. Leaving bridge, moving to follow-up. Thanks everyone. :pray:
